annotationRationale: Reflection matches the exterior circular segments with the interior pieces removed. Complementary areas give the result without requiring a separate sector calculation.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The construction is unambiguous without a supplied figure. The circumradius is 1 and the hexagon area is \(3\sqrt3/2\). Reflection removes inside the hexagon the same total segment area that originally lay outside it, giving \(3\sqrt3-\pi\), choice B. No grading or choice contradiction exists.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The sector calculations in the references compute the same removed segments individually. They are useful variants of the same decomposition, but do not require a second retained method.
review.annotationCheck: Reflection and composite-area reasoning are correctly assessed. Regular polygons, triangle area, the Pythagorean theorem, and circle area are genuine supports. Removing sector area from the assessed concepts accurately reflects this method.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The six central triangles have angles 60 degrees and are equilateral, establishing radius 1. The height and hexagon-area calculations are correct. Each reflected cap stays in its corresponding central triangle, so the six interiors do not overlap. Thus \(S=\pi-H\) and the desired area is \(H-S=2H-\pi=3\sqrt3-\pi\).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solutions 2 and 4 support the claimed whole-area balance. The candidate supplies original prose and additional radius, height, and nonoverlap explanations. The nonofficial, source-informed-original classification is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening identifies the useful invariant under reflection. The central-triangle construction, radius derivation, height calculation, and two complementary-area equations make the argument reconstructible without an additional diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_132, cnm_p150, cnm_266, and cnm_p192 directly describe reflection, area subtraction, the hexagon-circle relationship, and circle area. The question-level supports cnm_p148 and cnm_174 also accurately record the explicit triangle and height calculations.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact 轴对称的性质, 组合图形的面积, 正多边形与圆, and 圆的面积 links support the immediate concepts. The question-level 三角形的面积 and 勾股定理 supports also fit. Construction and axis-finding portions are not assessed.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: G-CO.B.6 partially supports reflection congruence; 8.G.A.1 and its subparts and G-CO.A.2 offer only related transformation properties, without experimental verification or function comparisons here. The 6.G.A.1 and 7.G.B.6 links support polygon decomposition, while 3.MD.C.7/7d do not cover curved caps. 7.G.B.4 supports circle-formula use, but G-GMD.A.1's derivations are absent. cnm_266's G-CO.A.3 and G-CO.D.13 links do not cover this radius calculation. These are limits of national coverage.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate concepts are supported and the assessed reflection/composite-area pairing captures the decisive strategy. Sector-area knowledge is unnecessary for this route.
